scope: Bounded primary-source prerequisite review of Wshobson staged originals, index rows 1-20, in original index order; initial selected runtime: offline non-root standard-library Python. Paper-cohort curation only; no runtime eligibility determination.
linked_reference_caveat: Only the indexed original bodies were read, through the existing guarded display helper. Linked references, example projects, external documentation, helper implementations named by sources, dependency packages and licenses outside these bodies were not inspected or fetched. Their existence, completeness, compatibility and reuse rights remain prerequisites, not established results.

sources.workflow: Audit AI-generated project code for failure paths, orphaned resources, edge cases, invented dependencies and architectural drift; relate findings to surrounding project conventions.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs the actual generated changes, surrounding modules, dependency manifests and installed-version/API evidence. The body names no executable audit helper or pinned toolchain; language-specific cleanup behavior must be understood.
sources.offline_assessment: A genuine offline public-code task is reviewing a licensed repository change and correcting a demonstrated missing cleanup or error path. Standard-library Python could support a Python target, but React or other language targets need their own compatible tools. No target repository or reproducible failure is supplied; this reading proves no eligibility or fix.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need an independently established defect oracle, failure-injection and resource-lifecycle regression tests, and a reviewer checking findings against actual library versions. Confirm target and helper licenses; body licensing is not established here.

sources.workflow: Design idempotent and observable Airflow DAGs, connect tasks, configure retries and scheduling, and validate operators and deployment behavior.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Example imports Airflow DAG, PythonOperator and EmptyOperator, with datetime utilities; needs an Airflow version compatible with these imports and schedule semantics. Real extraction logic, datasets, DAG project, operator/provider dependencies and any service configuration are not supplied. Detailed patterns are delegated to an unread local reference.
sources.offline_assessment: Offline review or repair of a real public DAG and its retry/schedule configuration is a legitimate code subtask. Parsing and exercising the DAG requires Apache Airflow beyond standard-library Python. The example extraction returns a fixed record count and is not an implemented ETL workload; scheduler, retries, sensors and production operation remain unverified.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independently authored DAG-import, dependency-graph, schedule, retry and idempotence tests over actual input fixtures, then separately controlled scheduler/integration checks if that scope is claimed. Verify Airflow/provider compatibility and repository, dependency and reference licenses.

sources.workflow: Design or review REST resources and HTTP semantics or GraphQL schemas, with versioning, pagination, validation, structured errors and rate limits.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs a concrete API contract, domain entities, consumer requirements and existing implementation or schema. OpenAPI/Swagger, GraphQL schema tooling and DataLoaders are named practices rather than a delivered implementation; versions and target-language dependencies are unspecified. Detailed examples are in an unread reference.
sources.offline_assessment: Editing a real public API specification or implementation to repair a documented contract defect is an actual offline subtask. Standard-library Python can process JSON specifications and some Python code, not establish GraphQL execution, rate-limit enforcement or cross-client compatibility. No real contract, client corpus or acceptance oracle is supplied.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent contract/schema validation and consumer-facing conformance tests for methods, errors, pagination and deprecation, plus domain review. Runtime performance and monitoring need separate evidence. Confirm licenses and compatible schema/server tooling for the chosen public project.

sources.workflow: Localize an active macOS connectivity incident across LAN, DNS, upstream path and application/service domains using bounded observations; report confidence and unknowns without remediation.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Requires the affected application/process, exact incident destination, time pattern and trustworthy local-target or previous-address evidence. Full workflow uses macOS scutil and nettop plus dig, ping, traceroute and curl; networkQuality is optional. Needs authorized live measurements, not invented destinations; detailed interpretation is in an unread reference.
sources.offline_assessment: Analysis of a supplied, sanitized real incident capture is an offline evidence-review subtask; a real public diagnostic script might also be repaired if supplied. No public-code implementation or incident measurements are staged in this body. Offline Python cannot reproduce active macOS link, resolver or application traffic behavior, and unrelated probes would not verify the incident.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independently labeled incident evidence that distinguishes observed, inferred and unknown results, with ambiguous ICMP and DNS cases. Any full workflow claim needs a separately authorized macOS/network verifier, not this shared host. Check evidence redistribution and any implementation/helper licenses.

sources.workflow: Build data-quality validation using Great Expectations, dbt tests and contracts; run suites across tables, report failed expectations and fail the pipeline on validation failure.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs actual tables, schemas, datasource configuration, contracts, expectation suites and checkpoints. Great Expectations and dbt are external dependencies with no compatible versions pinned. The body references DataQualityPipeline without defining it and contains a detached report-method fragment; the unread detailed reference cannot be assumed to complete it.
sources.offline_assessment: Repairing an actual public validation pipeline or its rules against licensed data fixtures is a real offline code task. Simple data checks can be written with Python, but replacing the stated frameworks with a toy checker would not validate this workflow. The supplied fragment is not a complete runnable pipeline under standard-library Python.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need the complete implementation/helpers, version-matched framework tests, independently labeled passing/failing tables, cross-table and freshness cases, and checks of report/failure behavior. Verify schema/data provenance, framework API compatibility and licenses before any runtime decision.

sources.workflow: Turn analytics into a setup/conflict/resolution narrative, use visuals and contextual comparisons, and finish with stakeholder-relevant recommendations and an action.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs actual licensed data, baseline/context, audience goals and the intended report or presentation format. No plotting package, code helper, data file or scoring rubric is supplied; detailed worked examples are deferred to an unread reference.
sources.offline_assessment: A real public analytics report generator could be revised offline with its actual dataset, and source-supported narrative writing itself can be offline. This body supplies neither public code nor the data and does not establish a runnable task. Standard-library Python can aggregate suitable input but cannot prove visual clarity, causal claims or persuasive impact.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent reconciliation of every numerical claim to data and a human rubric for audience fit, uncertainty, narrative and chart honesty. Identify actual generator/visualization dependencies and their compatibility; verify data, chart, helper and source reuse rights.

sources.workflow: Analyze installed dependencies and peer compatibility, plan staged major upgrades, migrate APIs, validate unit/integration/visual/end-to-end behavior and prepare rollback and update automation.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs a real project with manifests, lockfiles, baseline tests and changelog/migration evidence for chosen versions. Examples depend on Node/npm or yarn, React-related packages, glob, jscodeshift, test utilities and optional Cypress, Renovate or Dependabot. Compatibility matrix and check function are illustrative/incomplete; codemod inputs and migration transforms must be available locally.
sources.offline_assessment: A genuine offline public-code subtask is a pinned dependency migration using a locally complete source/dependency corpus and existing regression tests. Python alone can inspect manifests or edit code, not execute Node builds or establish React compatibility. Network audits, package downloads, automation services and staged rollout are outside this review; no migration has been demonstrated.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent before/after regression results, peer-dependency resolution, meaningful navigation/visual tests and verified rollback from a recoverable project state. The body includes placeholder assertions and broad textual replacements, so inspection is not validation. Check exact dependency/codemod versions, transform behavior and licenses.

sources.workflow: Explain PluginEval static lint, experimental judge and Monte Carlo layers, weighted composite scores, penalties and depth-based badges; distinguish signals from human-validated quality.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs actual PluginEval engine/CLI code, skill/plugin files and score fixtures to check implementation. Quick depth is described as static and model-free; deeper layers require model access and an LLM extra. Linked rubrics, improvement guidance and trace-program documentation are unread; no installation version or package license is established.
sources.offline_assessment: A public-code offline subtask could validate composite renormalization, the anti-pattern penalty and null/unmeasured fields against the actual engine using deterministic fixtures. Standard-library Python may support numeric recomputation, but the engine and dependencies are not provided here. Model self-predictions, response length and nonempty output are explicitly not proven triggering or quality; badges do not establish eligibility.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent numeric test vectors and code-to-spec checks for missing layers, plugin aggregation and thresholds. Human-labeled trigger/output evidence is required to validate the experimental measures; self-generated labels are not independent. Verify engine/helper licenses and compatible CLI dependencies; no model evaluation was run.

sources.workflow: Structure an async FastAPI application with injected database/auth services and use in-process ASGI tests with an async test database to verify a user-creation endpoint.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Explicit packages include FastAPI, uvicorn, pydantic-settings, SQLAlchemy asyncio at least version 2, asyncpg, PyJWT, pwdlib Argon2 and optional python-multipart; tests add pytest, pytest-asyncio, httpx and aiosqlite. Requires actual app, database helpers, models and endpoint implementation. Notes specify async fixtures for strict mode and ASGITransport for httpx 0.28 compatibility; detailed implementations are unread.
sources.offline_assessment: Repairing a real public app endpoint with local ASGI/SQLite tests is a substantive offline code task distinct from live PostgreSQL or deployment. Those dependencies are not standard-library Python, and the fixture imports an absent app. Existing snippets are requirements and a test sketch, not evidence that authentication or user creation works.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independently authored endpoint/schema/error/authentication tests, database lifecycle/isolation checks and a compatible pinned dependency set. Live database and service operation require separate verification if claimed. Confirm app, fixture/helper and dependency licenses; the linked implementation cannot be assumed available.

sources.workflow: Compose CI testing and matrix builds, container publishing, Kubernetes deployment, reusable workflows, vulnerability scanning and approval/notification steps.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs real repository source, package lockfiles and test/build scripts, workflow event/permission requirements and compatible action versions. Node examples use versions 18 and 20; Python matrix spans 3.9 through 3.12 and three operating systems. Full publishing/deployment needs runners, registry permissions, cloud and cluster configuration and service tokens; reusable workflow inputs/secrets must match.
sources.offline_assessment: Editing an actual public workflow to correct matrix, permissions or reusable-call wiring is an offline public-code subtask; inspecting YAML text does not execute CI. Standard-library Python lacks a YAML/GitHub workflow validator. Action downloads, image pushes, cloud deployment, scanners requiring services and notifications cannot be established offline; production deployment example still has placeholder commands.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent workflow-schema/expression validation, least-privilege/event tests and actual project build/test outcomes on the stated matrix in a separately authorized environment. Check action pin compatibility and licenses, input dependencies, approval behavior and non-placeholder deployment checks; no hosted workflow or token was used.

sources.workflow: Implement goroutines, channels and synchronization with context cancellation, sender-owned closure and graceful worker shutdown; detect race conditions and leaked work.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The quick start imports only Go standard packages context, fmt, sync and time, but requires a Go compiler/runtime. The best-practice errgroup is a separate dependency if used. Needs an actual concurrent project and workload plus compatible Go/module metadata; detailed pool/pipeline patterns are in an unread reference.
sources.offline_assessment: The included worker example is genuine Go code suitable for later local compilation, and a real public worker-pool defect could be repaired offline. Python standard-library availability does not supply a Go toolchain or prove goroutine lifecycle properties. The three one-shot sends and timeout example do not establish production pooling, fairness or race freedom.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent cancellation, blocked-send, channel-close and termination tests, Go race-detector evidence and bounded leak/stress checks on the real workload. Confirm Go version and any errgroup API compatibility, and licenses for source, target repository and dependencies.

sources.workflow: Author Grafana dashboard JSON with RED/USE metrics, panels, PromQL queries, namespace/service variables and alerts; provision dashboards as files or infrastructure code.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs Grafana with a compatible dashboard/alert schema, a Prometheus datasource and actual metric names, labels, histogram buckets and notification configuration. Provisioning also names YAML, Terraform and Ansible tooling/configuration. No dashboard runtime version, metric fixture corpus or authenticated deployment configuration is supplied.
sources.offline_assessment: A real public dashboard JSON can be edited and JSON-parsed offline with standard-library Python; this directly advances dashboard-as-code work rather than simulating Grafana. The body offers substantial JSON, but parsing does not verify PromQL results, legacy graph/alert compatibility, rendering, alert delivery or provisioning. Those behaviors remain unproven.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent dashboard-schema checks for the selected Grafana release and query fixtures with known rates/latencies, variable expansion and no-data/error cases, followed by separate rendering/alert verification. Confirm datasource/plugin and provisioning-tool compatibility plus dashboard, metric-data, helper and dependency licenses.

sources.workflow: Install Linkerd on Kubernetes, inject workloads, define route retry/timeouts and canary splits, apply authorization and advanced routing, and link/observe multiple clusters.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Explicitly needs a CLI compatible with the target cluster, kubectl, Linkerd CRDs/control plane and workloads/services. Resource schemas include ServiceProfile, TrafficSplit, Server, ServerAuthorization and HTTPRoute. Multi-cluster setup needs separate cluster configuration and reachability; optional viz extension supplies the monitoring/tap commands. API/CRD versions must match the installed release.
sources.offline_assessment: Editing a real public mesh manifest, retry budget or routing policy is an actual offline configuration-code subtask. Standard-library Python can inspect text, not validate Kubernetes/Linkerd YAML semantics or implement proxies. Installation, injection, mTLS, live traffic distribution and cross-cluster checks require separately controlled infrastructure; none is demonstrated by templates.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent version-specific CRD/schema checks and policy/route tests, plus later isolated cluster evidence for permitted/denied requests, retries, traffic weights, identity and multi-cluster behavior. Check manifest/helper/dependency licenses and the required mesh/Gateway API compatibility; no cluster commands were executed.

sources.workflow: Estimate TAM, SAM and SOM using top-down industry evidence, bottom-up customer/pricing calculations and value-theory willingness-to-pay assumptions.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs an actual market definition, product/geographic constraints, industry reports, customer-segment counts, pricing and competition/resource evidence. No calculator, dataset, formula implementation or validated input set is delivered; detailed worked examples are in an unread reference.
sources.offline_assessment: Offline calculation and reconciliation of real supplied market data is meaningful; a public market-model spreadsheet or code implementation could be repaired if provided. Standard-library Python can perform arithmetic, but the source is methodological and supplies no public-code target or market evidence. Recomputing invented numbers would be a proxy, not verified market sizing.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent provenance and date checks on market/customer inputs, expert review of SAM/SOM and willingness-to-pay assumptions, and an independently calculated sensitivity/cross-method reconciliation. Confirm data/report redistribution licenses and any actual calculator dependencies/licenses; no market claim is proven here.

sources.workflow: Decompose a monolith by capability or bounded context; choose synchronous/event communication, per-service data ownership, sagas and circuit-breaker/backoff/bulkhead resilience.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs the real application domain, existing monolith/services, interface/data ownership contracts and failure/consistency requirements. REST, gRPC, GraphQL, Kafka and RabbitMQ or SQS are alternatives, not universal mandatory dependencies. No concrete implementation, pinned stack or data workload is supplied; detailed patterns are in an unread reference.
sources.offline_assessment: A genuine public-code offline subtask could repair a specific saga compensation or circuit-breaker implementation in a supplied repository. Python standard-library tests may suit some local Python logic, but the body gives concepts rather than such code. Real broker delivery, service discovery, distributed consistency and failure isolation cannot be inferred from a diagram or local mock.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent domain/contract review and fault/recovery tests for the actual implementation, with separate distributed-integration evidence for ordering, retries, compensation and isolation. Establish compatible chosen broker/protocol/runtime versions and source, helper, data and dependency licenses before choosing a runtime.

sources.workflow: Build adaptive native SwiftUI layouts, navigation and feature cards using semantic colors/type and SF Symbols; check accessibility, state restoration, device interaction and performance.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Requires an iOS SwiftUI project, Apple platform SDK/compiler and compatible deployment targets: NavigationStack is labeled iOS 16+, newer Tab syntax iOS 18+, and symbol effects iOS 17+. Needs real app models/views referenced by examples, visual assets and device/simulator configurations; hardware and VoiceOver are needed for the expressly requested experience checks.
sources.offline_assessment: Editing a real public SwiftUI view or the included FeatureCard is an actual offline source-code subtask, not an assurance of native behavior. Standard-library Python cannot build or render SwiftUI. Layout, Dynamic Type, Dark Mode, VoiceOver, gestures, haptics and on-device performance remain unverified; the body specifically says simulator coverage is insufficient.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent compilation/API availability checks and UI/accessibility tests across deployment targets, iPhone/iPad sizes and content sizes, plus real-device haptic/performance review. Confirm Apple tool/asset rights and public project/dependency licenses; no Apple runtime or hardware was accessed.

sources.workflow: Plan mutual certificate authentication through service sidecars, root/intermediate/workload CA hierarchy, gradual strict-policy migration, expiry monitoring and certificate rotation.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs actual services/proxies, a chosen compatible mesh/TLS stack, trust roots, workload identities, policy and certificate lifecycle requirements. Concrete configuration templates are delegated to an unread reference. No deployable manifests, certificate fixtures, issuance helper or pinned implementation are included; do not use live keys as review input.
sources.offline_assessment: Offline inspection or repair of a real public trust-policy configuration with non-secret certificate fixtures would be a substantive subtask. Python has TLS facilities, but the body supplies no concrete code or fixtures, and substituting a small handshake demo would not verify mesh migration or rotation. Full chain validation, enforcement and cross-cluster identity are not proven.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent certificate-chain/identity acceptance and rejection vectors, expiry/rotation tests, and separate controlled mesh migration/enforcement verification. Clarify the distinction between the shown self-signed root and the warning about self-signed workloads. Establish mesh/CA helper compatibility and source/dependency/fixture licenses.

sources.workflow: Implement ERC-721/ERC-1155 minting, supply/payment/ownership rules, off-chain or on-chain metadata and EIP-2981 royalty interfaces for NFT assets.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Examples specify Solidity ^0.8.0 and OpenZeppelin contracts including Counters and multiple inheritance overrides; exact compatible OpenZeppelin/compiler versions must be selected rather than assuming latest. Needs missing supporting imports/inheritance/helpers such as Strings, Base64 and getRarityName, real metadata/assets and a local compiler/EVM test harness. Some snippets carry SPDX MIT; that does not establish the entire document or asset license.
sources.offline_assessment: Compiling, repairing and locally testing actual public NFT contracts is a genuine offline public-code task if the compiler, dependencies and EVM are available. Standard-library Python cannot execute Solidity semantics. OnChainNFT is incomplete and generateSVG returns a placeholder; NFTWithRoyalties uses onlyOwner without shown ownership inheritance. Minting, marketplace support and royalty enforcement are unproven, not reasons for automatic exclusion.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent compiler/interface-conformance tests, access-control/supply/payment boundary and receiver-callback/reentrancy checks, batch edge cases and metadata/royalty vectors in an isolated EVM. Verify version-specific inheritance overrides and source, dependency and media licenses. Marketplace and hosted metadata behavior need separate authorized evidence; no chain or wallet was used.

sources.workflow: Decompose feature work into vertical, horizontal or hybrid streams; assign exclusive file ownership, freeze interface contracts and integrate results through shared or separate branches.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs an actual feature specification, repository structure, ownership map, contracts, tests and a coordination mechanism for implementers/lead. TypeScript interfaces refer to domain types that the target project must define. Real multi-agent implementation requires a capable harness and suitable version-control/build tools; linked team/communication guidance is unread.
sources.offline_assessment: An offline plan or repair of real public ownership/contract artifacts can advance the stated workflow, but this body does not provide an implementation to run. Standard-library Python cannot stand in for parallel agents or prove integration safety. A fabricated ownership game would be a proxy; no agents or branches were created during review.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent checks for overlapping file ownership, unresolved domain types and consumer/provider contract agreement, followed by real integration regression tests. A separately authorized coordination trace is required to claim parallel workflow behavior. Confirm harness/type-tool compatibility and target, helper and reference licenses.

sources.workflow: Capture and analyze traffic, identify protocol boundaries/signatures and fields, document a specification, and validate parser/generator understanding; later sections also describe active fuzzing and replay.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Requires authorized traffic samples and known scenarios. Named tools include Wireshark/tshark, tcpdump, mitmproxy/Burp, Scapy and Boofuzz; live capture/interception/replay adds privileges, permissions and network targets. Binary/encryption and dissector/documentation helpers are in two unread references. Must obtain licensed sanitized captures and complete parser inputs without accessing real secrets.
sources.offline_assessment: Offline analysis of real supplied captures and repair of a public parser/dissector is a substantive code subtask distinct from live capture or fuzzing. Standard-library Python could process a specified binary format with complete fixtures, but the body supplies no actual capture or full parser; Scapy is external. Replaying traffic, interception and contacting fuzz targets are neither needed nor permitted here.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independently decoded, provenance-checked multi-session captures, known message boundaries/endianness/checksum cases and malformed-input tests, cross-checked against a separate parser or specification. Confirm parser/tool/version and capture licenses. Active behavior would require an isolated authorized target and independent safety verification; no traffic was generated.

source_reader: Delegated complete-original-body review; exact cohort selection, original hashes, line totals, disjoint IDs and citation bounds independently reconciled by parent.
status_scope: Only original-body prerequisites; linked references, concrete tasks and runtime evidence remain distinct.
